argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Mixed: some premises explicit, others implicit in textual analysis

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High: acknowledges counterarguments and integrates them
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: all points serve the central thesis
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate: relies on interpretive claims about Plato and post-modernism

explicit_definitions_given: Literary criticism: interpretation of texts as revelatory
Post-modernism: methodology of textual interpretation with anti-Platonic metaphysics

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges metaphysical opposition between Plato and post-modernism, then resolves via Hegel
objections_raised: Plato's metaphysics are otherworldly, post-modernism rejects this
Elenchus appears in early dialogues, not literary criticism

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Textual evidence from Plato, historical survey of post-modernism, philosophical analysis

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Continental philosophy, hermeneutics, history of philosophy

structural_organization.structure_type: Three-part dialectic: thesis (Plato's literary criticism), antithesis (post-modernism's metaphysical opposition), synthesis (Hegel's redefinition of god)

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that Plato's true methodology is literary criticism, not the elenchus, aligning him methodologically with post-modernism. However, their metaphysics are opposed. Hegel resolves this by redefining the divine as humanity, making texts revelatory again, thus restoring Plato's methodology while transforming its metaphysical basis.

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Moderate: leaves final judgment to reader
